How to type tab (quick guide)
fret.stringOne note. 3.5 = 3rd fret, 5th string (A). Strings: 1 = high E … 6 = low E
:4 :8Set the note length for the notes that follow (4 = quarter, 8 = eighth)
3.2.2Length for one note only (here a half note)
(0.5 2.4)Notes played together (chord)
|Bar line
rRest
5.3{h}Effect on a note: h hammer/pull, sl slide, v vibrato, pm palm mute
3.2.4{d}Dotted note
\tempo 90Tempo (put above the . line, with \title "…")

FretLab Beta — Quick Start

  1. Open a Guitar Pro file (.gp, .gp5, .gpx…), MusicXML (.musicxml/.mxl) or tab text — or drag a file onto the page.
  2. Press ▶ (or Space). The red cursor follows the music; the fretboard shows where to play.
  3. Slow it down with the Speed slider. Pitch stays the same.
  4. Loop a hard spot: drag across bars in the tab to select them, then turn on 🔁 Loop.
  5. Speed Trainer: select bars, set start/step/stop, click Start. Speed rises each time the loop repeats.
  6. Edit right on the tab: click a beat on a string line. Type a fret number (two digits work: 1 then 2 = 12). ←→ move between beats, ↑↓ move between strings. Option/Alt+↑/↓ moves the note to the next string at the same pitch. I insert beat · Del delete · R rest · +/− note length · . dot · Esc done.
  7. Sounds: under each part's name, pick its instrument and drag its left/right position. 🎛 Separate the parts does this for every part at once. Sound choices are saved in the .gp file; Ctrl+Z undoes them. For richer sounds, 🎹 Load sound bank lets you pick a bigger .sf2 file (remembered on this device).
  8. Transpose / Capo (left panel) shifts the parts on screen, or adds a capo and re-frets so it sounds the same.
  9. 🎮 Game (or G): drag across a few bars, then press Game. The notes fly toward a glowing "play now" line and the bars repeat until you stop. V switches between Tab lanes and Fretboard views, F is full screen, [ ] change speed. 🎤 Feedback is off until you turn it on; then the microphone listens and the notes you play light up (single notes: pitch and timing; chords: timing only). The loop never stops.
  10. 🎙 Practice logs practice time automatically and records audio or video to turn in. While recording, the music stays on screen and a small camera box sits in the corner. After pressing Record, take your time to get ready — press Space for a 4-beat count-in, and recording starts with the count. With 🎯 Score my playing, notes turn green when on time, early/late notes get an orange/purple ghost note, the score goes in the file name, and the video ends with the marked-up music. Turn recordings in by following your class procedure.
  11. Lessons in other tunings (try lesson 7, Drop D) show a 🎯 Tune now reminder. Teachers set a part's tuning in Tuning (lesson setting) on the left, then 💾 Save.
  12. 🎯 Tuner (T): guitar, bass and 5-string bass; standard, drop, down-tuned and open tunings. Play one string at a time. Tap a string to hear it and lock onto it.
  13. Write / Edit opens a text editor. Type tab like 0.6 2.5 2.4; the score updates as you type.
  14. Export to .gp (opens in Guitar Pro 8 / TuxGuitar), .mid, or .txt. Print → "Save as PDF" for handouts.

No sound? Tap ▶ once (browsers need a tap before playing sound). On iPhone/iPad, turn off the silent switch or update iOS. Check the volume and Bluetooth speakers or headphones. Press 🔊 Test: if you hear a beep but no music, wait a few seconds for the sounds to load. Always download the file first; don't open it from a Drive, email or class-website preview.

Beta limits: no MusicXML export yet; no copy/paste of bars yet; the built-in sound bank is small (load a bigger .sf2 for better sound).

Built with alphaTab (MPL-2.0), Bravura font (SIL OFL), Sonivox soundfont (Apache-2.0).

🎙 Practice Log & Recorder

Record yourself

🎯 Scoring: notes turn green when you play them on time. Early notes get an orange ghost note, late notes a purple one, and missed notes a red ring. Single notes are checked for pitch and timing; chords for timing only. Score = on time 100%, early/late 50%, missed 0%.
When you press Record, this window closes so you can read the music and the camera turns on — but nothing records yet. Get your guitar ready, then press Space (or ▶ Start on the small camera box) for a 4-beat count-in. Recording starts with the count. Press ■ Stop on the box when you're done.
Turn it in: 1 type your name above · 2 record · 3 watch/listen back · 4 💾 Save (your score is in the file name) · 5 turn in the saved file — plus the practice log .csv or results picture if your teacher asks — by following your class procedure for submitting assignments. Recordings stay on this device until you hand them in.
